source_text: Nec de peccatorum differentia modo tractandum est, sed credendum omnino nullo modo nobis ignosci ea, quae peccamus, si nos inexorabiles ad ignoscenda peccata fuerimus. itaque credimus et remissionem peccatorum.
orientation: Augustine is concluding his treatment of the forgiveness of sins within the creed, warning that God's forgiveness of us is conditional on our forgiving others.
pass_a_gloss: And it is not now to be treated about the difference of sins, but it must be believed entirely that in no way are those things forgiven to us, which we sin, if we have been unyielding for forgiving sins. And so we believe also the forgiveness of sins.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the creedal article
Captures the refusal to be moved toward forgiving others
Strong negation matching the Latin emphasis
Reinforces the absoluteness of the belief required

pass_b_english: Nor is this the moment to discuss the differences among sins. What we must believe, entirely and without exception, is that the sins we commit will in no way be forgiven us if we remain unyielding when it comes to forgiving sins. And so we believe in the forgiveness of sins.
